name: desktop-user-flow-registry
purpose: Defines the end-user and developer-superadmin flow for making the agent platform usable as installable desktop software.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry before designing desktop screens, onboarding, installer behavior, first-run setup, workspace selection, CLI capability checks, or user-facing task execution flows.
how_to_read: Read product_principles first to understand the usability bar.
Read install_flow and first_run_flow before adding installer or desktop shell code.
Read home_information_architecture and task_run_flow before designing app navigation.
Read developer_superadmin_flow when exposing internal configs, traces, agents, logs, and validation tools.
Read failure_recovery_flows before adding background processes, CLI adapters, local services, or updates.
update_triggers: The app adds real installer, updater, sidecar, local service, or CLI execution.
View mode, install mode, work mode, notification, CLI adapter, or orchestration behavior changes.
A usability test, user session, or support issue shows friction in install, first run, task start, result review, or recovery.

structure_rules.rule: First run must reach a readable workspace dashboard or demo dashboard before asking the user to configure every optional integration.
structure_rules.reason: A long setup wizard blocks value discovery and repeats the same clarification bottleneck the platform is meant to reduce.

structure_rules.rule: User mode shows the smallest useful task flow; developer and superadmin details are available through explicit view mode selection and advanced drawers.
structure_rules.reason: The platform has many internal artifacts, but an installable product must not make a new user understand all of them before starting work.

structure_rules.rule: Missing optional CLIs, notification channels, or advanced validators must create setup guidance and disabled capabilities, not block unrelated work.
structure_rules.reason: Waiting for one unanswered setup question should not stop other usable flows.

structure_rules.rule: The desktop app must ask the user to open or create a workspace path and explain what will be indexed before scanning or executing commands.
structure_rules.reason: Installable software needs a stronger privacy boundary than a developer-local repository run.

structure_rules.rule: Every task run should show active step, elapsed time, waiting decisions, produced artifacts, verification, and recovery action.
structure_rules.reason: The product value is reducing repeated work, so the user must be able to see what the platform is doing and where it is blocked.

structure_rules.rule: The desktop app may orchestrate Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, browser tools, or local CLIs through adapters, but it must not hard-code one assistant runtime as the product identity.
structure_rules.reason: The platform concept is a reusable operating layer over many tools, not a wrapper around one vendor.

field_guide.meaning: User-facing design principles for the installable product.
End-user path from download to first launch.
Initial in-app setup and time-to-first-value path.
How a user starts, monitors, interrupts, reviews, and saves a task.
How user-answerable questions are captured, batched, answered, and resumed.
How Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Claw Code, and future AI CLIs are selected, run, paused, merged, and observed.
Advanced flow for platform builders who need internals, configs, traces, and validators.
How missing dependencies, failed commands, blocked decisions, stale snapshots, and update failures recover.

product_principles.principle: Open an existing workspace or create a new one in one obvious path.
product_principles.design_implication: The first screen prioritizes workspace open/create/demo, not settings.

product_principles.principle: Optional integrations are discovered and can be configured later.
product_principles.design_implication: Capability cards show status, missing setup, and a setup button without blocking the dashboard.

product_principles.principle: Agent work should be visible as a timeline with evidence, artifacts, timing, decisions, and next action.
product_principles.design_implication: Task detail uses a run timeline instead of a hidden terminal-only process.

product_principles.principle: User mode is task-oriented; developer and superadmin mode expose platform internals.
product_principles.design_implication: The app reuses view_mode but does not treat UI hiding as security.

product_principles.principle: Workspace selection, secrets, external CLI use, and network behavior are explicit.
product_principles.design_implication: The app explains local indexing and never bundles private data or tokens into installers.

product_principles.principle: Multiple AI CLIs can run in parallel, but the platform owns task state, questions, artifacts, and verification.
product_principles.design_implication: The UI shows CLI sessions as supervised lanes in one timeline instead of unrelated terminal windows.

product_principles.principle: Starting work should feel like a native IDE run surface, not a long web settings page.
product_principles.design_implication: The Run tab begins with Run Configuration, Services, Problems, and status-bar controls before deeper panels.

product_principles.principle: Useful CLI output should become structured records with provenance, validation, and retention policy.
product_principles.design_implication: The user sees durable artifacts, summaries, decisions, and reusable knowledge candidates rather than only raw logs.

install_flow.user_goal: Get the installer or development build.
required_behavior: show supported OS and version
show signature/notarization status when production-ready
link privacy and local-data behavior
distinguish user install from developer setup
avoid admin prompts unless a selected installer target requires them
install app without bundling secrets or private workspace data
leave rollback/uninstall path documented

install_flow.user_goal: Open the app and understand what to do next.
required_behavior: prioritize Open Workspace, Clone Workspace, Create Workspace, and Demo Workspace
postpone optional integrations
offer view mode selection with user mode as the simple path and superadmin as the builder path

first_run_flow.notes: A workspace path is required before real repository data is indexed. Demo mode is allowed when no workspace is ready.
Explain what folders, generated snapshots, history, and configs will be read.
Developer and superadmin developer modes are visible but framed as advanced product-building modes.
Only required workspace problems block. Optional capability gaps become setup cards.
This is the first-value moment. The user sees projects, recent history, active agents, and next actions.

Show projects, recent work, active tasks, and next actions.

Start a task with goal, project, work mode, output type, and optional notification.
Show progress, timing, agents, artifacts, decisions, and verification.
After the platform is already open, select Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Claw Code, or future CLI guest lanes and preview process graph constraints.
Inspect supervised terminal output and edit source files from a governed workspace surface.
Collect pending user questions without blocking unrelated work.
Browse summaries, traces, evaluations, commits, and generated artifacts.
Configure workspace, optional CLIs, notifications, secrets, and privacy.
Expose raw configs, validators, release gates, and platform health for builders.

measurement_targets.target: A new user should reach a dashboard or demo dashboard without configuring optional integrations.
measurement_targets.measurement: elapsed time from app launch to dashboard arrival

measurement_targets.target: A user should be able to start a guided task after workspace confirmation and readiness scan.
measurement_targets.measurement: elapsed time from dashboard arrival to task preflight

measurement_targets.target: A user-answerable question should block only dependent task lanes.
measurement_targets.measurement: number of independent lanes paused by a single pending decision

measurement_targets.target: A failed or paused CLI lane should not lose the whole task run when independent lanes have produced usable artifacts.
measurement_targets.measurement: percentage of multi-CLI runs where independent lane outputs remain reviewable after one lane pauses or fails

measurement_targets.target: Meaningful CLI output should become structured events, artifacts, decisions, or reusable knowledge candidates.
measurement_targets.measurement: ratio of accepted terminal-derived records to raw retained scrollback

measurement_targets.target: Missing optional CLIs or notification channels should not block core dashboard and history viewing.
measurement_targets.measurement: percentage of optional setup failures that remain capability-scoped

acceptance_checks: A user can understand the difference between installed app usage and repository developer setup.
A first-run path exists for Open Workspace, Create Workspace, and Demo Workspace.
Optional CLI and notification setup can be deferred.
Task execution shows active phase, elapsed time, evidence, artifacts, decisions, and verification state.
The platform-first app opens before any AI CLI and owns the durable task state, decision inbox, artifacts, validation, and UI authority.
AI CLI orchestration can show Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode, and Claw Code as optional guest adapters without making any one CLI or commercial assistant host mandatory.
A user can choose a task pipe preset and initialize several optional CLI lanes from one task intake, with stdin init, stdout/stderr capture, decision inbox routing, and merge gate edges visible.
Interactive CLI questions route to decision inbox and pause only dependent lanes.
Terminal output is visible in lane context, but durable platform state is stored as structured records with retention and redaction policy.
Source editing has a planned open-source editor surface and does not require writing a custom editor from scratch.
Developer and superadmin developer views expose internal configs and release gates without cluttering user mode.
Failure recovery is defined for unreadable workspace, missing optional CLI, pending user decision, stale snapshot, and update failure.
No real token, private snapshot, or browser session is bundled into installer artifacts.
The Agents screen includes AgentCore-style production blueprints backed by public AWS sources.
A blueprint application changes runnable task input and Agent Core input, not only documentation text.
A user can create an agent proposal from a selected AgentCore-style blueprint without manually filling every Agent Core field.
